formulation: Isoparametric 10-node tetrahedra, 4-point quadrature. Small-strain incremental associated von Mises plasticity, backward-Euler radial return and consistent tangent. Work-conjugate displacement control with unknown load multiplier; all loads scale together.
symmetry: Full solid in part.step; mesh is quarter body X>=0,Y>=0 where [X,Y,Z]=ROT*[x,y,z]. ROT is +45deg about z. At Y=0 uY=0; at X=0 uY=uZ=0 (antisymmetry in bending). J2 invariance under stress sign change allows antisymmetric quarter. Mesh and exported displacements use original physical frame.

physical_groups.10: continuous steel, shared nodes on all region interfaces

extraction: Largest computed equilibrated load factor at large work-controlled displacement; plateau checked at final increments. See actual curves and mesh convergence in refinement.json.

field_schema.equivalent_plastic_strain: element x 4, accumulated sqrt(2/3)*norm(plastic strain increments), final
field_schema.reaction_N: node x 3, final internal minus external nodal force, original frame; unconstrained entries are equilibrium residuals
field_schema.quadrature_coordinates_mm: element x 4 x 3 physical integration locations in original frame; tetra barycentric rule diagonal 0.5854101966 and off-diagonal 0.1381966011
field_schema.displacement_mm: step x node x 3 original frame
field_schema.force_reference_N: node x 3 assembled equivalent nodal reference loads in original frame
field_schema.fixed_mask_solver_frame: node x 3 boolean essential BC mask in X Y Z
field_schema.stress_Mandel_MPa: element x 4 quadrature points x [XX,YY,ZZ,sqrt2 XY,sqrt2 YZ,sqrt2 ZX], final state, rotated solver frame

limitations: Four-point integration and quarter symmetry; no geometric nonlinearity, no hardening. Finite displacement plateau is an approximation to asymptotic limit. The very large formal displacements used to approach the plateau do not update geometry; they are a numerical limit-load device, not a prediction of geometrically nonlinear deformation.
